paper.title: On Interpolating Experts and Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: m-MAB (arms partitioned into K groups; pulling an arm reveals losses of its whole group)
unmapped: feedback graph is a disjoint union of K cliques of sizes m_1,...,m_K (N = sum m_k arms)
the learner knows the group sizes vector m
settings.definition_quote: In the problem of $\*m$-\MAB, there are $N$ arms. The arms are partitioned into $K$ groups and the $k$-th group contains $m_k$ arms. ... The adversary chooses a loss function $\ell^{(t)}\in [0,1]^N$; The player incurs loss $\ell^{(t)}(A_t)$ and observes the losses of all arms in the group containing $A_t$. ... We assume the player knows $\*m$ and $T$ in advance

unmapped: feedback graph is a disjoint union of K cliques of sizes m_1,...,m_K
the learner knows the group sizes vector m and the target accuracy epsilon
settings.definition_quote: Each pull of an arm can observe the losses of all arms in the group. As usual, the goal is to identify the best arm (the one with minimum $p_i$) with as few rounds as possible. ... an $(\eps, \delta)$-probably approximately correct algorithm ... can find an $\eps$-optimal arm with probability at least $1-\delta$.

unmapped: learner knows a clique cover (V_1,...,V_K) of the graph

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit with graph feedback containing disjoint non-adjacent strongly observable subgraphs (lower bound)
settings.definition_quote: Let $G=(V,E)$ be the feedback graph. Assume that there exist $K$ disjoint sets $S_1,\dots ,S_K\subseteq V$ such that each $G[S_k]$ is a strongly observable graph with a self-loop on each vertex; there is no edge between $S_i$ and $S_j$ for any $i\ne j$.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit with weakly observable feedback graph (lower bound)
settings.definition_quote: Assume that $V$ can be partitioned into $K$ disjoint sets ... for every $k\in [K]$, each $G[V_k]$ is observable; ... there exists a $t_k$-packing independent set $S_k$ in $G[V_k]$ such that every vertex in $S_k$ does not have a self-loop; there is no edge from $V_i$ to $S_j$ for any $i\ne j$ in $G$.

algorithms.name: Two-Stage Algorithm for m-MAB (two-stage OSMD: Tsallis entropy over groups, negative entropy within groups)
PAC algorithm for m-BAI via reduction to m-MAB (run Algorithm 1, output arm sampled from empirical pull frequencies)

symbols.L_m: sum_{k=1}^K log(m_k+1), m_k = size of group k

source.label: thm:ub-m-MAB
source.quote: There exists an algorithm such that for any instance of $(m_1,\dots,m_K)$-\MAB, any $T>0$ and any loss sequence $\ell^{(0)},\ell^{(1)},\dots,\ell^{(T-1)} \in [0,1]^N$, its regret is at most $c\cdot \sqrt{T\cdot \sum_{k=1}^K\log (m_k+1)}$, where $c>0$ is a universal constant.

results.notes: Theorem 8 (thm:ub_clique) states the same bound for Algorithm 1 explicitly. Regret is E[sum losses] minus best arm's loss against a fixed loss sequence.

source.label: thm:lb-m-MAB
source.quote: For any algorithm $\+A$ of $(m_1,\dots,m_k)$-\MAB, for any sufficiently large $T>0$, there exists a loss sequence $\ell^{(0)},\ell^{(1)},\dots,\ell^{(T-1)}$ such that the regret of $\+A$ in $T$ rounds is at least $c'\cdot \sqrt{T\cdot\sum_{k=1}^K \log (m_k+1)}$, where $c'>0$ is a universal constant.

results.notes: Proved via stochastic Bernoulli(1/2) / Bernoulli(1/2-eps) instances (Lemma 21) and the BAI reduction.

tuning: run Algorithm 1 for T* = (2500c)^2 sum_k log(1+m_k)/eps^2 rounds

source.label: thm:ub-m-BAI
source.quote: There exists an $(\eps,0.05)$-PAC algorithm for $(m_1,\dots,m_K)$-\BAI which pulls $T\le c\cdot \sum_{k=1}^K\frac{\log (m_k+1)}{\eps^2}$ arms where $c>0$ is a universal constant.

results.notes: Deterministic number of pulls; correctness with probability 0.95.

source.label: thm:lb-m-BAI
source.quote: There exists an instance $\@H$ such that for every $\tp{\eps, 0.05}$-PAC algorithm $\+A$ of $(m_1,\dots,m_K)$-\BAI with $\eps\in \tp{0,\frac{1}{8}}$, the expected number of pulls $T$ of $\+A$ on $\@H$ satisfies $\E{T} \ge c'\cdot\sum_{k=1}^T\frac{\log (m_k+1)}{\eps^2}$ ... Moreover, we can pick $\@H$ as the one in which each arm follows $\!{Ber}(\frac{1}{2})$.

results.notes: Sum upper index 'T' in the paper is a typo for K. Lemma 20 gives the explicit form E[T] >= sum_k c1 log(m_k+1)/(2 eps^2) (if N>=2), and per-group E[T^(k)] >= c1 log(m_k+1)/eps^2; Lemma 14 is the single-group (full-information) case.

symbols.L_m: sum_{k=1}^K log(m_k+1), m_k = sizes of cliques in a clique cover (V_1..V_K) of G

conditions: G has a self-loop on each vertex
G contains a (V_1,...,V_K)-clique cover with |V_k| = m_k
tuning: Algorithm 1 run on G' obtained by ignoring edges between cliques

source.label: cor:ub-graph-bandit
source.quote: Let $G$ be a feedback graph with a self-loop on each vertex. If $G$ contains a $(V_1,\dots,V_K)$-clique cover where $\abs{V_k}=m_k$ for every $k\in [K]$, then the minimax regret of bandit with graph feedback $G$ is at most $c\cdot \sqrt{T\cdot\sum_{k=1}^K\log (m_k+1)}$ for some universal constant $c>0$.

results.notes: Bound on minimax regret, achieved by Algorithm 1 on the clique-cover subgraph.

symbols.L_S: sum_{k=1}^K log(|S_k|+1) over the disjoint sets S_k

conditions: there exist disjoint S_1..S_K with each G[S_k] strongly observable with self-loops on each vertex
no edge between S_i and S_j for i != j

source.label: thm:lb-graph-bandit-strongly
source.quote: Let $G=(V,E)$ be the feedback graph. Assume that there exist $K$ disjoint sets $S_1,\dots ,S_K\subseteq V$ such that each $G[S_k]$ is a strongly observable graph with a self-loop on each vertex; there is no edge between $S_i$ and $S_j$ for any $i\ne j$. Then for any algorithm $\+A$ and any sufficiently large time horizon $T>0$, there exists some loss sequence on which the regret of $\+A$ is at least $c'\cdot \sqrt{T\cdot\sum_{k=1}^K\log {(\abs{S_k}+1)}}$

results.notes: Graph G itself is not required to be strongly observable in the statement; the proof section assumes strongly observable G. Remark: also extends to loopless clique giving Omega(sqrt(T log N)).

symbols.W_S: sum_{k=1}^K max(log|S_k|, |S_k|/t_k), S_k a t_k-packing independent set of loopless vertices in G[V_k]

conditions: V partitioned into V_1..V_K with each G[V_k] observable
each G[V_k] contains a t_k-packing independent set S_k of vertices without self-loops
no edge from V_i to S_j for i != j

source.label: thm:lb-graph-bandit-weakly
source.quote: Let $G=(V,E)$ be the feedback graph. Assume that $V$ can be partitioned into $K$ disjoint sets ... Then for any algorithm $\+A$ and any sufficiently large time horizon $T>0$, there exists some loss sequence on which the regret of $\+A$ with feedback graph $G$ is at least $c'\cdot T^{\frac{2}{3}}\cdot \tp{\sum_{k=1}^K\max\set{\log {\abs{S_k}}, \frac{\abs{S_k}}{t_k}}}^{\frac{1}{3}}$ for some universal constant $c'>0$.

results.notes: Confirms conjecture of He & Zhang 2022; for disjoint union of K loopless complete bipartite graphs gives Omega(T^{2/3}(sum log m_k)^{1/3}).
